name: Ascendant Development
description: Defines Ascendant expression across universal developmental stages without converting orientation into personality.

content.coreRule: Development changes the flexibility, coherence, and awareness of orientation; it does not change the Ascendant's identity as a reference frame.

functionalPattern: Uses a habitual orientation automatically
Treats first salience as final meaning
Positions the self before recognizing the counterpart
Responds strongly to environmental mismatch
learningTaskComponents: Observe which cues become immediately salient
Notice how the frame changes after contact begins

functionalPattern: Controls presentation rigidly
Masks when the preferred orientation feels unsafe
Withdraws if self-positioning cannot be controlled
Treats misunderstanding as identity threat
requiredConditions: explicit exposure, shame, or safety evidence
learningTaskComponents: Allow the environment to provide corrective information

functionalPattern: Experiments with different ways of entering situations
Uses feedback to refine presentation
Practices updating orientation
Begins coordinating self-position and relational awareness
learningTaskComponents: Sample context before fixing the frame
Track which contexts require different entry strategies

functionalPattern: Establishes a coherent initial frame
Updates orientation as contact develops
Uses presentation without identity reduction
Maintains self-position while recognizing the counterpart
learningTaskComponents: Use the ruler function without replacing the angle
Let orientation become more relationally informed

functionalPattern: Moves between self-side and relationship-side orientation fluidly
Uses first contact as provisional information
Coordinates embodiment, perspective, and context without rigidity
Allows orientation to support rather than define identity
developmentalContribution: Creates coherent entry without overfixing identity
Allows presentation to remain functional and context-sensitive

crossStageRules.rule: The same orientation domain may use different surface verbs at different stages.
Masking, bracing, and performance require explicit defensive evidence.
Integrated Ascendant expression may still use deliberate presentation.
Healthy orientation does not imply social approval or accurate first impressions.
No stage may introduce a semantic domain absent from approved Ascendant vocabulary.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Reference-frame vocabulary only. Psychology and development qualify orientation but do not redefine the Ascendant as total personality, appearance, mask, or independent actor.
